- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction to smooth out overreaction.
- In 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price peaks in late period (last 7-10 days); increase forecast tail end by 1-3% to capture momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; match forecast slope to sentiment trend direction.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33), model often drifts toward historical mean; use sentiment as signal to avoid mean reversion trap.
